# A dock commit builds a hidden stand-in per item and destroys it unused

## Context

Measured 2026-09-04 at `dev@205bc52f8a` while checking D#18150's "header object permanence" step before it became a ticket (receipt: https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/18150#discussioncomment-18289767). Header chrome is already instance-stable across every commit class. What every commit does destroy is a set of components that never reach the DOM.

Live latest-open sweep: checked the latest 20 open issues at 2026-09-04T13:28Z; no equivalent found (#18208 is the Workstation's override of the item-only refresh; #18236, closed not-planned, was the comparator premise). A2A claim sweep over the last 30 messages: no competing claim; lane claimed 13:27Z.

## The Problem

Unit tier, a two-node document with three items, every `component.Base` construct and destroy counted with its creator stack:

| commit | change class | components destroyed | of which stand-ins |
|---|---|---|---|
| `setActiveItem` (a tab click) | topology | 8 | 3 |
| `setItemLocked` | itemFlags | 3 | 3 |
| `addTab` | topology | 9 | 4 |
| `closeItem` | topology | 10 | 3 |
| `setActiveItem` on the already active item (a no-op) | topology | 8 | 3 |

The stand-ins are one `Neo.create({module: Component, header, hidden: true})` **per document item per commit**, created hidden, never mounted, then destroyed. On the `itemFlags` path they are the whole cost. A consumer with twelve items pays twelve constructions and destructions per lock click, for a DOM delta of one class.

## The Architectural Reality

- `Workspace#refreshDockWorkspace` hands `projectDockModel` an item resolver that constructs a stand-in for every item (`src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:3796–3802`) through `createProjectionPlaceholder` (`:1562–1568`); the adapter calls it from `LayoutAdapter.projectItem` (`src/dashboard/dock/projection/LayoutAdapter.mjs:915–930`) via `context.resolveComponentRef(componentRef, item, itemId)`, without the node id.
- For a **retained** tab node the reconciler discards the whole projected tabs config behind a geometry placeholder (`Reconciler.prepareTabChromeProjection`, `src/dashboard/dock/projection/Reconciler.mjs:271–312`), so the stand-ins built for its items never enter a parent. The staged path then retires them (`:407–420`): *"Pane placeholders inside a discarded config for a retained tab node never enter a parent. Retire them now; only genuinely new tab nodes need projected placeholders for pairing."* The stable path retires them at `:252–255`. Both sweeps are the reconciler's contract towards any caller that hands it a full map — `DockProjectionReconciler.spec.mjs:379–436` asserts it directly — so they stay; on the workspace path they become no-ops.
- `reconcileTabChrome` treats a missing stand-in as a normal state: `resolve(itemId)` prefers the live pane (`:720–726`) and materialises a new one only when nothing is live (`:764–814`). Retained nodes reach that branch on every commit today, because their stand-ins were already destroyed.
- Stand-ins ARE load-bearing for a **new** tab node: the staged container is built from the config, and the stand-in's index pairs the projected tab button with the live pane that replaces it (`:774–789`).

## The Fix

Construct a stand-in only for an item whose tabs node is not retained — a caller-side change; the reconciler is untouched.

- `LayoutAdapter.projectTabsNode` passes its `nodeId` into `projectItem`, which passes it as a fourth argument to `context.resolveComponentRef`.
- `refreshDockWorkspace` collects the current shell's tab node ids (`Reconciler.collectProjectedTabs(currentShell)`) before projecting; its resolver returns `null` for an item in a retained node, so `projectItem` falls through to the item's persisted `blueprint` when present, otherwise to `createPlaceholder(itemId, item)` — a config either way, nothing constructed — which the reconciler discards with the tabs config as before.
- Docblocks of `createProjectionPlaceholder`, `projectItem` and the `resolveComponentRef` option say when a stand-in exists and why.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target surface | Source of authority | Proposed behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `LayoutAdapter.project({resolveComponentRef})` callback | `LayoutAdapter.projectItem` (`src/dashboard/dock/projection/LayoutAdapter.mjs:915–930`) | Called as `(componentRef, item, itemId, nodeId)`; `nodeId` is the tabs node the item projects into and is `undefined` on the rail-reveal path. A 1–3-argument consumer is unchanged: the extra argument is ignored. A `null` answer falls through to `item.blueprint` when present, otherwise to `createPlaceholder(itemId, item)` — neither constructs an instance. | Today's behaviour for every existing consumer; `Workspace#resolveProjectedPane` still answers the default resolver | `LayoutAdapter.mjs` option and parameter JSDoc; `Workspace#createProjectionPlaceholder` docblock | `test/playwright/unit/dashboard/DockProjectionStandIns.spec.mjs`: zero stand-ins for retained nodes across four commit classes; exactly one for the single item of a `splitNode`-minted node |
| `Workspace#createProjectionPlaceholder(itemId, item, componentRef)` | `Workspace#refreshDockWorkspace` item resolver (`src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:3796–3812`) | Invoked only for an item inside a tabs node the current shell does not render; a retained node's items never reach it. Signature and return unchanged. | An override still shapes every stand-in that IS created | `createProjectionPlaceholder` docblock | same spec — the lock arm asserts zero invocations, the split arm exactly one |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — `setItemLocked` on a two-node fixture destroys **zero** components (today: 3), measured through a `component.Base` destroy counter in a unit arm.
- [ ] **AC-2** — `setActiveItem`, `addTab` and `closeItem` construct **zero** stand-ins for items whose tabs node is retained; `createProjectionPlaceholder` is called exactly once per item of a **new** tab node (a `splitNode` that mints one), so pairing in `reconcileTabChrome` is unchanged.
- [ ] **AC-3** — the header chrome census holds: tab container, header toolbar, tab buttons and action buttons keep their instance ids across all five commit classes above.
- [ ] **AC-4** — the reconciler is not modified; the source delta is the resolver predicate, the node id parameter and their docs, with no forwarding layer or second code path.
- [ ] **AC-5** — no regression against the exact base: `DockWorkspace`, `DockLockAction`, `DockProjectionReconciler` and `DockLayoutAdapter` unit suites stay green; every `examples/dashboard/crossWindow` and Workstation dock journey arm that is green on the base commit is green on the branch, and any arm red on the base is recorded with a durable owner rather than claimed green.

## Out of Scope

- The staged shell itself (edge-zone and split containers, the splitter, the two projection placeholders) built on every topology commit — that is `retainTopology` as the default admission request and waits on D#18224's rail reconcile decision (cut 2 on D#18150).
- The reconciler's placeholder sweeps: they are its contract towards direct callers and stay.
- Any change to `toolbar.Base#syncActions` or `headerActions` handling: header permanence is already true and measured.
- The tear-out cluster.

## Avoided Traps

- **Skipping stand-ins for items that merely have a live pane.** A live pane moving into a *new* node still needs the stand-in for button pairing (`:774–789`); the retention of the NODE is the correct predicate, and the reconciler's own comment names it.
- **Deleting the reconciler's retire sweeps as "dead code".** They are dead on the workspace path after this change, but `DockProjectionReconciler.spec.mjs:432` asserts them for a caller that hands in a full map; deleting them changes a static utility's contract for one caller's convenience.
- **Fixing the comparator.** #18236 tried to make `isEqual` treat functions by identity and was closed not-planned; the churn here is constructed instances, not change detection.

## Decision Record impact

`aligned-with ADR 0029` — same-instance projection is the ADR's rule; this removes constructions that never became instances of anything visible. No schema or wire change.
